vectors.description: fetch stream header (type 0x05) with one object (flags 0x1c: GROUP_ID_DELTA, OBJECT_ID_DELTA and PRIORITY present, subgroup mode 0b00); the first object's deltas are absolute values
fetch stream with two objects (Ascending group order); the second uses pure delta encoding (flags 0x00) — Object ID is prior + 1 within the same group

fetch stream where the second object starts a new group via GROUP_ID_DELTA (flags 0x0c). In Ascending order the new Group ID is prior + delta + 1, and the Object ID is the Object ID Delta whenever a Group ID Delta is present

fetch stream where the second object carries an Object ID Delta but no Group ID Delta (flags 0x04). Section 11.4.1.1: "When the Group ID Delta field is not present, the Object ID is the prior Object's ID plus the Object ID Delta if present" — so this is prior + delta (2 + 4 = 6), not the delta itself (4), and not prior + delta + 1 (7). The first Object's Object ID is 2 so that the delta-alone reading differs. The Group ID Delta present case one row above resolves Object ID differently, which is what makes this pair worth having: a decoder that reads Object ID Delta the same way in both branches passes one and fails the other

fetch stream where the second object starts a new group via Group ID Delta but carries no Object ID Delta (flags 0x08). Section 11.4.1.1: "If Object ID Delta is not present, the Object ID is the prior Object's ID plus one, regardless of which group it belongs to." So the Object ID continues 7 → 8 across the group boundary rather than restarting at 0, which is the reading a decoder is most likely to get wrong. Ascending order, so the Group ID is prior + delta + 1 = 1

fetch stream read in Descending Group Order (group_order 2, the FETCH's GROUP_ORDER): Object 0 of Group 10, then a second object with flags 0x0c and Group ID Delta 1. Section 11.4.1.1: "If the Group Order is Descending, the Group ID is the prior Object's Group ID minus the (Group ID Delta + 1)." So its Group ID is 10 - (1 + 1) = 8, where Ascending would give 12

fetch stream with an End of Non-Existent Range marker (Serialization Flags 0x8C, encoded as the two-byte varint 808c) as the first record, so its Group ID and Object ID are absolute. Section 11.4.1.2: on an End of Range record the Group ID and Object ID fields are present and Subgroup ID, Priority and Properties are not. Object Payload Length is not on that exclusion list and Figure 29 marks it mandatory, so it is present and encoded as 0; omitting a field the figure requires is what desynchronises a fetch stream. The draft does not settle this.
fetch stream with an End of Unknown Range marker (Serialization Flags 0x10C, encoded as the two-byte varint 810c), group_id 5, object_id 10

fetch stream with an End of Timed-Out Range marker, new in draft-20 (Serialization Flags 0x20C, encoded as the two-byte varint 820c) as the first record, so its Group ID and Object ID are absolute. Every Object between the last serialized Object, if any, and {5,10} inclusive timed out: the relay's FILL_TIMEOUT budget ran out. Draft-19 reported all of these as Unknown gaps (0x10C) and had no distinct marker. All three markers carry the low bits 0x0C, the ordinary "both deltas present" pattern, so the two fields that follow occupy the Group ID Delta and Object ID Delta slots of Figure 29. Section 11.4.1.2: on an End of Range record the Group ID and Object ID fields are present and Subgroup ID, Priority and Properties are not. Object Payload Length is not on that exclusion list and Figure 29 marks it mandatory, so it is present and encoded as 0; omitting a field the figure requires is what desynchronises a fetch stream. The draft does not settle this.

fetch stream with an object followed by an End of Timed-Out Range marker that is not the first record. Section 11.4.1.2: "the Group ID and Object ID fields are present". They are absolute: the delta rules of Section 11.4.1.1 cover "an Object other than the first", and a Serialization Flags value of 128 or more is not read as flag bits (Section 11.4.1: "When less than 128, the bits represent flags"). Draft-23 changed this ("Delta encode FETCH End of Range indicators"). So the End of Timed-Out Range marker is {6,9}; read as an ordinary delta it would be Group 5 + 6 + 1 = 12

fetch stream where an ordinary object follows an End of Timed-Out Range marker and references the prior Object. Section 11.4.1.2 fixes what "prior" means across a marker: prior Group ID and prior Object ID come from the marker ({6,9}), while prior Subgroup ID and prior Priority come from the last actual Object before it (priority 128). The trailing object's flags are 0x00, so its Group ID is 6, its Object ID is 10, its Subgroup ID is 0 and its Priority is inherited

fetch stream whose first object, {5,0}, carries a PRIOR_GROUP_ID_GAP=2 property (flags 0x3c: PROPERTIES, PRIORITY, GROUP_ID_DELTA and OBJECT_ID_DELTA). A fetch stream carries no Object Status: status is only present on subscription-delivered objects. Section 10.8: "An Object has a Prior Group ID Gap larger than the Group ID." That makes the Track malformed (Section 12.1), so the Group ID is at least 2
fetch stream with the DATAGRAM flag set (flags 0x5c). The two least significant bits are ignored and no Subgroup ID is present, because an Object with Delivery Mode Datagram has none
fetch stream with an explicit subgroup_id (flags 0x1f: subgroup mode 0b11, so the Subgroup ID field is present, plus PRIORITY, GROUP_ID_DELTA and OBJECT_ID_DELTA)

fetch stream whose first record carries Serialization Flags 0x8D, encoded as the two-byte varint 808d. Values below 128 are flag combinations and draft-22 Table 8 defines exactly three values at or above it — 0x8C End of Non-Existent Range, 0x10C End of Unknown Range and 0x20C End of Timed-Out Range. "Any other value 128 or greater is a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION." The remaining bytes are those of the fetch-end-of-non-existent-range vector, which decodes
vectors.error_detail: 0x8D is neither a flag combination below 128 nor one of the three End of Range markers

vectors.description: truncated fetch header — missing request_id
vectors.error_detail: unexpected end of input while reading request_id

vectors.description: fetch stream with Objects 0 and 1 of Group 5 carrying Prior Group ID Gap 2 and 3. The second object's flags (0x20) leave its Group ID, Object ID and Priority to the Object before it. Section 10.8: "A Group contains more than one Object with different values for Prior Group ID Gap." That makes the Track malformed (Section 12.1)
vectors.error_detail: two Objects in Group 5 carry different Prior Group ID Gap values

vectors.description: fetch stream with an object in Group 9 and then Object 0 of Group 10 carrying Prior Group ID Gap 1 (flags 0x2C; its Group ID Delta of 0 is the prior Group ID plus 1). Section 10.8: "An endpoint receives an Object with a Prior Group ID Gap covering an Object it previously received." The gap covers Group 9, which this stream delivered first. Section 2.1.2: "The Object is known to exist. From this state, it can transition to not existing, but not vice versa." The two conflict, so whether the Track is malformed is ambiguous, and the decoder does not refuse this

fetch stream with Objects 8 and 9 of Group 3, the second carrying Prior Object ID Gap 1. The second object's flags (0x20) leave its Group ID, Object ID and Priority to the Object before it. Section 10.9: "An endpoint receives an Object with a Prior Object ID Gap covering an Object it previously received." Section 3.2.1: "Within each group, objects are sent in Object ID order; subgroup ID is not used for ordering." The gap covers Object 8, delivered just before. Section 2.1.2: "The Object is known to exist. From this state, it can transition to not existing, but not vice versa." The two conflict, so whether the Track is malformed is ambiguous, and the decoder does not refuse this

fetch stream with Object 0 of Group 1 carrying Prior Group ID Gap 2. Section 10.8: "An Object has a Prior Group ID Gap larger than the Group ID." That makes the Track malformed (Section 12.1), which an endpoint detects from this Object alone
vectors.error_detail: Prior Group ID Gap 2 is larger than Group ID 1

vectors.description: fetch stream with Object 1 of Group 3 carrying Prior Object ID Gap 2. Section 10.9: "An Object has a Prior Object ID Gap larger than the Object ID." That makes the Track malformed (Section 12.1), which an endpoint detects from this Object alone
vectors.error_detail: Prior Object ID Gap 2 is larger than Object ID 1

vectors.description: fetch stream with Object 0 of Group 5 carrying Prior Group ID Gap 1 twice. Section 10.8: "An Object contains more than one instance of Prior Group ID Gap." That makes the Track malformed (Section 12.1), which an endpoint detects from this Object alone
vectors.error_detail: an Object contains more than one Prior Group ID Gap

vectors.description: fetch stream in Descending Group Order (group_order 2) with Object 0 of Group 10 carrying Prior Group ID Gap 2, then Object 0 of Group 9 (flags 0x0c; its Group ID Delta of 0 is the prior Group ID minus 1). Section 10.8: "An endpoint receives an Object with a Group ID within a previously communicated gap." Group 9 is within the gap Group 10 communicated. Section 2.1.2: "an endpoint can receive an Object after it has already recorded that the Object does not exist" and "This is not a protocol error and the Track is not malformed." The two conflict, so whether the Track is malformed is ambiguous, and the decoder does not refuse this
